next_step: Complete Dedicated POC performance run (canary) and finalize pricing SLA; legal to confirm DPA by 3/20
notes: Background: mid-market SaaS (product analytics + in-app assistant). Heavy interactive chat plus periodic re-ranking for search results. Currently on internal transformer-based models for offline embeddings; exploring hosted first then Dedicated for production latency and throughput.
Discovery call (2026-01-12) - AE Maya intro. Primary contact: Head of Product (Lena Hart). Quote: 'We need predictable latency and a plan if the model starts missing intent.'
Demo (2026-01-28) - showcased Hosted API chat + embeddings. Team liked streaming and function-calling. Early concerns: token cost and how batching affects p95 latency for UI.

Pricing convo (2026-02-03) - high level reserved capacity math. Finance asked for ARR estimate and committed throughput to justify Dedicated pool. Follow-up pricing deck shared: /drive/pricing/azurebend_redwood_pricing_v2.pdf
Security & procurement (2026-02-11) - security questionnaire sent, SOC2 + SSO required. Legal asked for DPA + audit log retention policy. Security FAQ draft in Drive.

POC kickoff (2026-02-18) - scope: Dedicated small pool (2xA100 equiv) for 3-week canary. Goals: validate p95 latency <200ms for chat at 100 concurrent users and 300 RPS embeddings pipeline. Carlos (SE) running perf harness. Fireflies: ff_2026-02-10_azb_kickoff

Canary plan notes: vertical canary by route (chat-chatbot route only) -> gradually shift 10% -> 50% -> 100%. Fallbacks: auto-route to Hosted API model variant of same family if Dedicated node saturates; cross-region failover to us-west-2 if us-east-1 has issues. Rollback plan: instant traffic cut to hosted with circuit-breaker and alerting on >5% error rate or latency spike >2x baseline.

POC interim (2026-03-04) - found a ~25% latency increase for long-context (8k tokens) sequences under batching. SE recommended KV-cache tuning + smaller batch window for chat route. Jira tickets created: INF-3124 (kv-cache investigation), INF-3191 (batch window tuning)
Customer quotes: 'We like the dedicated runway but need a clear rollback and cross-region route — can't have the in-app assistant go down during peak.'
Current sentiment: cautiously optimistic. Product team pushing to close before Q2 budget freeze. Legal and Security are the gating items.
timeline: 2026-03-10 - POC status review; legal requested DPA updates
requirements_summary: Workload: interactive chat assistant (primary), embeddings for semantic search and reranking (secondary).
Latency targets: chat p95 <200ms for 2-4k contexts; acceptable degradation to <350ms for 8k contexts with mitigation plan.
Throughput targets: sustained 300 RPS for embeddings pipeline during nightly enrich; 100 concurrent chat users during daytime peak (bursty).
Cost sensitivity: mid-market finance wants predictable committed cost vs variable hosted spend; exploring reserved Dedicated pool with burst policies.
Model preferences: open/Redwood-verified models; appetite for quantized variants if quality preserved. Preference to route to smaller, cheaper variants for low-priority background reranking jobs.
Routing/fallback needs: canary rollout for Dedicated, auto-fallback to hosted model variant, region failover (us-east-1 -> us-west-2), automated rollback triggers tied to latency/error SLOs.
Observability: token-level cost breakdown, per-route latency dashboards, tracing for requests older than 2s.
Operational controls: ability to pin model version, A/B rollout controls, and pre-configured rollback policy templates.
Security/compliance: SSO (SAML/Okta), SOC2 required, audit logs + 1-year retention, KMS for key management, data residency in US only for now.
poC_details: Duration: 3 weeks (small Dedicated pool) + 1 week extended mitigation run
Scope: chat route canary -> expand to embeddings batch jobs, verify autoscaling and burst behavior
Canary percentages: 0% -> 10% -> 50% -> 100% over 48-72 hour windows with health checks
Fallbacks: per-route fallback to hosted_api variant; circuit-breaker with backoff; alerting to on-call (pager) at 5% error rate or 2x baseline latency
Rollback: manual and automated options. Automated triggers for rollback include sustained p95 >2x baseline or semantic quality degradation measured by prompt set evals
Metrics to collect: p50/p95/p99 latency, tokens per request, cache hit rate, error rate by status code, cost per 1k tokens
